prompt: How has Falcon (FALC) been doing on velocity and say/do over its recent sprints? I'm trying to decide how much to commit for next sprint.
final_text:
Falcon finishes about **32 points a sprint** (about 10–11 items), but it delivers only about **79% of what it commits to**. The gap between those two numbers is the useful part for planning.

**The last six sprints (story points)**

| Sprint | Dates | Velocity | Predictability | Say/do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.24 | Sep 30 – Oct 13 | 34 | 0.95 | 0.85 |
| 2026.22 | Sep 2 – Sep 15 | 27 | 0.78 | 0.66 |
| 2026.21 | Aug 19 – Sep 1 | 38 | 1.00 | 0.92 |
| 2026.20 | Aug 5 – Aug 18 | 21 | 0.65 | 0.57 |
| 2026.19 | Jul 22 – Aug 4 | 31 | 0.89 | 0.80 |
| 2026.18 | Jul 8 – Jul 21 | 40 | 1.00 | 0.94 |
| **Average** | | **31.8** (±6.5) | **0.88** | **0.79** |

- **Velocity** is all the work finished during the sprint. **Predictability** is velocity divided by what was committed. **Say/do** counts only the committed work that got finished.
- 2026.23 was an IP sprint, so it's left out of these numbers.
- Counting items instead of points gives the same picture: 10.5 items a sprint and 0.77 say/do.

**What stands out**

1. **They've been committing about 35 points.** That figure is worked out from velocity and predictability, so treat it as approximate. In sprints that didn't hit 100%, they finished only about 18–31 of the points they planned. Say/do is lower than predictability, which means some finished work was added after the sprint started and replaced committed work.
2. **Good and bad sprints alternate.** Each strong sprint (40, 38, 34) is followed by a weak one (31, 21, 27). The data doesn't say why. If that pattern holds, it tilts against next sprint. Ask the team whether the misses come from carry-over, unplanned work coming in, or people being out, because each needs a different fix.
3. **The latest sprint was solid.** It reached 0.95 predictability and 0.85 say/do, so things may be improving, but one sprint isn't enough to show a trend.

**My recommendation: commit about 30 points (roughly 9–10 items).**
- That sits a little under the 32-point average and well under the ~35 they've usually planned, which should push say/do toward 90%.
- If you want a high-confidence commitment, 26–28 points is about what they reliably finished in their weaker sprints.
- If you know this sprint will bring unplanned work, keep the commitment at 30 or below. Leave that room open rather than filling it with stretch items.
- Adjust for known capacity changes such as holidays or people out. These numbers assume a normal team.

final_text:
Here's how the Raptors split their effort from July 1 to September 30, 2026. The Raptors are a team of teams made up of Falcon, Osprey and Kestrel, and the figures cover 412 completed work items.

| Project | Share of effort | Items | Main contributor |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No project** | **32.7%** | 135 | Kestrel (82 items) |
| Mobile Experience Refresh (MOBX) | 26.4% | 109 | Osprey (87 items) |
| Payments Reconciliation (PAYRC) | 18.9% | 78 | Kestrel (62 items) |
| Self-Service Onboarding (ONBRD) | 15.2% | 63 | Falcon (50 items) |
| Billing Export Retirement (BILLX) | 6.8% | 28 | Falcon (22 items) |

All four projects are in the Digital Commerce portfolio.

**What stands out**
- **A third of the work isn't linked to any project.** That's the biggest single slice, larger than any one project. Kestrel did about 61% of it (82 of 135 items). That could be support work, maintenance or tech debt, or it could be work that should have been linked to a project and wasn't.
- **Each project has one main team.** Osprey did about 80% of the Mobile Experience Refresh work, Kestrel about 80% of Payments Reconciliation, and Falcon about 80% of both Onboarding and Billing Export.
- **The three teams did similar amounts of work:** Falcon 34.2%, Kestrel 34.2% and Osprey 31.6% of the total.

**How this was measured:** Shares use the "team effort" measure, which weighs each team's work in its own sizing unit before combining them. That avoids adding story points from one team to item counts from another. The split comes out the same as a simple count of completed items, so the percentages hold up either way. The report only names each project's largest contributor, so I can't give a full team-by-project grid. I can pull the reports for Falcon, Osprey and Kestrel separately if you want that.

prompt: Is Osprey's backlog in good enough shape to plan the next PI from? Mostly I want to know how many weeks of runway they have.
final_text:
I can't give you a reliable runway figure. Wayd wouldn't grade it: Osprey finished only 7 backlog items in the last 90 days, and the check needs at least 10. I asked for a 180-day lookback instead, but the response still covered only the last 90 days (19 Jul – 16 Oct), so a longer window didn't help.

**A rough figure, not a graded one:** 7 items finished in about 13 weeks is roughly 0.5 items a week. At that pace the 18 open items would last around **33 weeks**. That's past the 26-week "too long" line. But 7 items is too few to rely on, and the backlog is growing, so read it as "probably plenty of runway," not as a number to plan with.

**Is the backlog ready to plan a PI from? Not yet. Fix these first:**

| Check | Grade | What's behind it |
|---|---|---|
| Missing Estimate | **Unhealthy** (28%) | 5 of 18 items have no estimate: MOB-232, 234, 236, 239, 242. Two of them are already in progress. |
| Net Flow | At Risk (1.29) | 9 items created vs 7 finished, so the backlog is growing faster than the team clears it. |
| Stale | At Risk (17%) | MOB-237, 241 and 244 haven't changed since 30 June. |
| No Parent | At Risk (11%) | MOB-234 and MOB-244 aren't linked to a parent item. |
| No Project | Healthy, one item | MOB-241 isn't on a project. |

**Worth raising at planning:**
- **All 6 in-progress items are assigned to Marcus Hale.** None of the other 5 team members has one. The WIP Load check counts work per team member, so it shows 1.0 and grades Healthy, but the work really sits with one person.
- None of the open items is in a sprint, and all 6 active ones were started on 5 October.
- In total the backlog is only 39 story points across 18 items, all in the "Offline-first mobile app" (MOB-150) work.

**Before PI planning, I'd suggest:**
1. Estimate the 5 items that have no estimate.
2. Decide whether to keep or close the 3 stale ones.
3. Spread the active work beyond Marcus.

If you want a firmer delivery number, I can run a throughput forecast to your PI end date. It uses the same thin history, though, so it will have the same weakness.
